_note: ST-00 canonical state map (roadmap parity-evidence §7). The named-region layout of the engine's ~18 MB save/working arena, so a divergent BYTE OFFSET in a captured save.dat (or a working-arena snapshot) resolves to (scope, bank, region, element, field) instead of a bare number. SOURCE OF TRUTH is src/save_bank.h + docs/findings/save-working-arena.md; every entry cites its #define / DAT_ address. This file is the MACHINE map (consumed by tools/parity/save.py's localizer + future ST-02 encoder); the prose model + the four state CLASSES are docs/reference/canonical-state.md. v1 covers the well-defined named fields; unmapped byte ranges resolve to 'bank N dword D (unmapped)', which is honest, not a guess. Extend as consumers surface field semantics — never invent a name for a byte whose meaning is unknown (roadmap ST-00 stop condition).

arena._geom: arena = [0x0b10 shared header][100 x 0x2dfc8 bank]. abs byte of bank N field-dword D = 0x0b10 + N*0x2dfc8 + D*4. The SAVE arena (DAT_056e5770, disk save.dat) and the WORKING arena (DAT_044e3798, live game state) share this exact layout; a save.dat is the save arena dumped verbatim (src/save_io.c write_arena_to).

policy.float: f32/f64 fields are compared by BIT PATTERN (the project's x87-invariant rule) — no epsilon. A named float region records elem_type so a report can print the value, but equality is over raw bits.
policy.pointer: the save/working arena carries NO pointers or OS handles — it is pure value data (a disk mirror). Every dword is a comparable value; there is nothing to normalize away.
policy.unknown_bytes: a byte range with no named region is class 'unknown': INCLUDED in a byte-exact comparison (never silently masked) and reported as 'unmapped'. Excluding a byte requires a named region with an explicit reason (none excluded in v1).
policy.checksum: each bank ends with an XOR-sum checksum at dword 0xb7f1 (save_bank_stamp_checksum). It is a pure function of the bank's content, so it only diverges when the content it covers already diverged — a checksum-only diff is impossible when content matches, and a checksum diff downstream of a content diff is a derived echo, not a second finding.

classes.persistent: on disk in save.dat; survives sessions (the save arena).
classes.volatile_deterministic: live game state the same layout holds in the working arena; reproducible under pinned inputs but not itself on disk unless committed. Fields tagged with working_alias double as this.
classes.unknown: byte-preserved but semantics not yet mapped.
